content:
Ari: Heads-up — noticed a ~2-3x tail latency bump on canary for long-context workloads after the merge landed last night (commit abc1d9e).
Ari: Quick tail snapshot from canary logs:
Ari: ```
2026-03-18T02:14:10Z model-serving-3 INF tail_lat_99=420ms prev_baseline=180ms
2026-03-18T02:14:12Z model-serving-3 INF kv-cache-hits=12 batch-size=1
```
Sasha: Ugh. Thanks for flagging. Any obvious CI failures?
ci-bot: perf/inference-ci — build #1285 failed: tail-latency threshold exceeded (99th=418ms > 250ms).
Jules: I ran a quick git bisection locally, looks like the change to kernel-selection heuristics in PR #4678 is suspicious — switches some models to the new tiled-kernel path for seq_len>1024.
Dana: That PR also changed the batching heuristic threshold, could make small batches go through a slower kernel. We need to confirm.
Ari: @Sasha can you run the reproduce perf test on master+revert locally? I've got a short repro script:
Ari: ```bash
# run perf harness
git checkout HEAD~1 # revert candidate
bazel run //perf:inference_bench -- --model redwood/longctx --seq_len 1536 --concurrency 4
```
Sasha: Running now — will record p99 and attach flamegraphs.
QA-Eng: Noted. If we end up reverting, we need a backport to release/v1.12 and a smoke ondedicated cluster.
Sasha: Quick update — revert of commit abc1d9e locally drops p99 back to 175ms. Flamegraph shows big time in tiled_kernel_dispatch.
Jules: OK that matches. Plan: open a revert PR to master, then cherry-pick revert to release/v1.12, run CI perf, and coordinate a small hotfix rollout.
Dana: I can open the revert PR and the backport. I'll use the release branch naming: release/v1.12-hotfix/kernel-revert-1930
Dana: Commands:
Dana: ```bash
git checkout -b revert/kernel-heuristics-1930
git revert --no-commit abc1d9e
git commit -m "revert: kernel heuristics change causing tail latency regression"
git push origin revert/kernel-heuristics-1930
gh pr create --base master --head revert/kernel-heuristics-1930 --title "Revert kernel heuristics change (abc1d9e)" --body "Revert due to tail latency regression on long-context workloads"
```
ci-bot: Created PR #4727 — perf/inference-ci triggered.
Sasha: Running the perf CI on the revert PR now.
ci-bot: perf/inference-ci — PR #4727 build #1286 passed: tail-latency p99=178ms.
Ari: Nice. Dana please cherry-pick the revert commit onto release/v1.12 and push a release PR.
Dana: Will do. Cherry-pick and create backport PR to release/v1.12 -> #4728.
ci-bot: release-ci — PR #4728 build #290: smoke tests queued.
QA-Eng: Once #4728 passes, I'll schedule a canary rollout on dedicated us-west-2 pool and run the workload for 30m.
Sasha: For the rollback verification, let's add a short perf check to the release job so we don't regress again: compare p99 against baseline and fail if >1.5x.
Jules: Agreed. I'll add a quick perf gate script to the release CI next.
Dana: Backport PR #4728 passed smoke and perf check (p99=182ms). Pushing patch to release branch now.
Dana: ```bash
git checkout release/v1.12
git cherry-pick <revert-commit-sha>
git push origin release/v1.12
```
Ari: After the canary warms up, roll to 10% of dedicated, monitor cost and tail latency, then full rollout if stable. @QA-Eng coordinate the 30m run.
QA-Eng: Canary run started at 03:12 UTC. Will post results at 03:45.
Sasha: Post-mortem note: PR #4678 added kernel routing fallthrough for tiled-kernel too aggressively. We should implement a perf test that exercises tiled dispatch for long-context and gate that path behind an opt-in flag until we have perf numbers.
Jules: I'll add the opt-in flag and a test in a follow-up PR and add the perf gate to CI.
QA-Eng: Canary 10% run complete — p99 stable ~180ms, no error uptick. :thumbsup:
Ari: OK, merge backport & cut hotpatch. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. Follow-up ticket: INF-981 add tiled-kernel perf gate + unit tests.
Sasha: Filing INF-981 now.
ci-bot: release-bot — hotfix release scheduled: v1.12.1-kernel-revert at 04:10 UTC.
Dana: I'll watch the rollout and have rollback steps ready if anything else pops up.
Ari: Great work, team. Keep an eye for related alerts in the next 24h.
